q: Consider the prohibition of forced labour: 1-It binds private persons. 2-It protects citizens only. 3-Payment below the statutory minimum wage has been held to amount to forced labour. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It protects all persons, not citizens alone.
why: The wage holding is what makes the provision operationally significant: the trigger is wages and debt, not physical restraint.
trapnote: Two limbs: it binds private hands, and it protects every person. Only the second is often missed.

q: On compulsory service imposed by the State, which statement is correct?
options: Impermissible in all circumstances, the prohibition on forced labour being absolute
Permissible only during a Proclamation of Emergency approved by both Houses of Parliament
Permissible for public purposes, without discrimination on grounds only of caste or class
Permissible for public purposes, discrimination on any ground being immaterial
expl: The exception is express and carries its own non-discrimination condition.
why: The word only in the constitutional text matters: discrimination must not rest on those grounds alone.
trapnote: An express exception with an express condition. Neither limb may be dropped.

q: On child labour: 1-The constitutional provision covers factories, mines and hazardous work. 2-The 2016 statute bars all employment below fourteen, with narrow exceptions. 3-The Constitution bars all employment below fourteen. Correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The constitutional provision is narrower than the statute.
why: Reading which instrument the question asks about is the whole skill here: the statute goes further than the Constitution.
trapnote: The statute is wider than the Constitution. Identify which instrument the statement describes.

q: On the freedom of religion, which statement is correct?
options: It extends to citizens only and is subject to public order, morality and health
It extends to all persons and is subject to public order, morality and health
It extends to all persons and is subject to public order alone
It extends to all persons and admits of no restriction whatever
expl: All persons, subject to public order, morality, health and other Part III provisions.
why: The rights-holder and the restriction grounds are tested together, and each wrong option varies one of them.
trapnote: All persons, and four heads of limitation including other provisions of Part III.

q: On State power over religious institutions: 1-It may regulate associated secular activity. 2-It may provide for social welfare and reform. 3-It may throw open Hindu institutions of a public character. Correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three powers are expressly saved.
why: The explanation to the provision extends the reference to Hindus to include Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists.
trapnote: Three express saving powers. The reference to Hindus is extended by an explanation.

q: On the prohibition of taxes for the promotion of religion, which statement is correct?
options: Both a tax and a fee for services are barred where religion is concerned
A tax is permitted where the legislature records a secular purpose for it
A tax appropriated for a particular religion is barred; a fee for services rendered is not
A fee for services is barred, though a tax is permitted where it is levied on all persons equally
expl: The distinction is between a compulsory exaction for promotion and a payment for services rendered.
why: The fourth option reverses the distinction entirely, which is the cleanest form of the error.
trapnote: Tax for promotion is barred. Fee for a service rendered is not. The distinction is the provision.

q: On religious instruction: 1-Wholly prohibited where the institution is maintained entirely from State funds. 2-Permitted with consent where the institution is aided. 3-Permitted without consent in a trust-established, State-administered institution. Correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three situations are accurately described.
why: Most material reduces this provision to two situations; there are four, and the trust-established one is the exception to the exception.
trapnote: Four situations, not two. Only the trust-established institution dispenses with consent.

q: On the right of minorities to administer educational institutions, which statement is correct?
options: Administration by a minority is sufficient, establishment being immaterial
The minority must both establish and administer the institution for the right to arise
Establishment by a minority is sufficient, administration being immaterial
The right arises wherever a majority of students belong to the minority
expl: Both limbs are required.
why: An institution merely administered by a minority, but founded by another, does not qualify.
trapnote: Both limbs are required. Neither establishment nor administration alone is enough.

q: Consider the unit for determining whether a community is a minority for educational purposes: 1-The unit is the State. 2-The unit is the country as a whole. 3-A community may be a minority in one State and not in another. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The State is the unit, which is why status can vary between States.
why: Reorganisation of States on linguistic lines is the reason the State was adopted as the unit.
trapnote: The State is the unit. The consequence is that status varies from State to State.

q: On the protection against denial of admission in a State-aided institution, which statement is correct?
options: It protects members of religious and linguistic minorities alone against such denial
It protects any person, citizen or otherwise, against such denial
It protects any citizen against denial on grounds only of religion, caste or language
It protects any citizen against denial on any ground whatever
expl: The protection is for any citizen, on the grounds specified.
why: Despite its placement among minority provisions, the protection is not confined to minorities.
trapnote: Placement among minority provisions does not confine the protection to minorities.

q: On the power to prescribe punishment for offences under the rights chapter: 1-It vests in Parliament. 2-It vests in a State legislature for State subjects. 3-It explains why the enforcement statutes are central. Correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The power vests exclusively in Parliament.
why: The exclusivity overrides the ordinary distribution of legislative powers for this limited purpose.
trapnote: A specific exclusive power defeats the general distribution for this purpose.

q: On restrictions applicable to members of the armed forces and forces charged with maintaining public order, which statement is correct?
options: A State legislature may do so for the forces it maintains within the State
Parliament may by law restrict or abrogate the application of the rights to them
The restriction may be imposed by executive order of the appropriate government
No restriction is permissible, the rights being available to all citizens
expl: The power is exclusive to Parliament and is exercised by law.
why: This is the provision of most direct personal relevance to a police candidate.
trapnote: Parliament alone, and by law. No State legislature and no executive order will do.

q: Consider the remedy for enforcement of Fundamental Rights before the Supreme Court: 1-It is itself a Fundamental Right. 2-It may be suspended as the Constitution provides. 3-Two articles may never be suspended. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three are accurate.
why: The remedy is itself a right, which is why its suspension requires express constitutional authority.
trapnote: The remedy is a right, it is suspendable by authority, and two articles remain beyond reach.

q: On the dispute concerning entry to a hill shrine, which statement reflects the position?
options: A 2018 decision permitted entry, and the matter is finally settled
A 2018 decision refused entry, and a reference remains pending
A 2018 decision permitted entry, and a larger-bench reference remains pending
The matter has never been decided by the Supreme Court in any proceeding
expl: The 2018 decision stands, but larger questions were referred in 2019 and remain undecided.
why: Treating the matter as settled is the commonest error in current material on this topic.
trapnote: Decided in 2018, referred in 2019, still pending. Do not present it as settled.

q: Consider a religious denomination: 1-It may manage its own affairs in matters of religion. 2-It may own and acquire property. 3-It administers its property free from any law. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Administration of property is subject to law.
why: The distinction between managing religious affairs and administering property is the operative one.
trapnote: Religious affairs are protected; property administration is subject to law.

q: On the right to conserve a distinct language, script or culture, which statement is correct?
options: It is available to religious and linguistic minorities alone and to no other section
It is available to any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture
It is available to any person residing in the territory of India
It is available only where the State has recognised the language concerned
expl: Any section of citizens may claim it, not minorities alone.
why: The marginal heading refers to minorities, which is what makes the second option persuasive.
trapnote: A marginal heading is not the provision. The text speaks of any section of citizens.

q: On compulsory acquisition of a minority institution's property: 1-The amount must not restrict or abrogate the right. 2-The provision was inserted by amendment. 3-It applies to all private institutions equally. Correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The provision is specific to minority educational institutions.
why: The third statement generalises a specific protection, which is the standard construction in this area.
trapnote: A protection written for one category does not extend to all private institutions.

q: On martial law and the rights chapter, which statement is correct?
options: Martial law automatically suspends the rights chapter in the area concerned
Martial law requires a proclamation by the President under the Emergency provisions
Parliament may indemnify acts done in connection with the maintenance of martial law
Indemnity may be granted by the State government for acts within its territory
expl: Indemnity requires a law of Parliament.
why: Martial law is not one of the three Emergencies and is dealt with in a separate provision.
trapnote: Martial law is separate from the three Emergencies and carries its own indemnity provision.

q: Consider: 1-Trafficking in human beings is prohibited by the rights chapter. 2-The prohibition is enforced through central legislation. 3-A State legislature may prescribe punishment for it. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Punishment for such offences may be prescribed by Parliament alone.
why: The exclusivity of the power is what makes the enforcement statutes central legislation.
trapnote: The prohibition is constitutional; the punishment is central. The two follow from each other.

q: On the employment of adolescents between fourteen and eighteen, which statement is correct?
options: The Constitution bars their employment in any occupation whatever
The 2016 statutory amendment bars their employment in hazardous occupations
No restriction applies to that age group under either instrument
The Constitution bars their employment in factories and mines alone
expl: The category of adolescents was created by the 2016 statutory amendment.
why: The category does not appear in the Constitution at all, which is what the wrong options obscure.
trapnote: The adolescent category is statutory. The Constitution speaks only of children below fourteen.
